question: Can the same two native applications, with one shared adapter for reasoning, general instructions and external actions, outperform untouched Base on new human requests while retaining the released tool behavior?
protocol: Train independently starting from the qualified two-pass typed checkpoint. No fitted weights, learned routes or logits from the closed folded, raw-language, dialogue-state or prior shared reasoning-and-action models. Preserve the frozen instruction sibling 8-bit prefix and the trained shared rank-32 final-layer Q/K/V/O adapter; continue that same adapter across both native applications. Fit 4402 actual response records: 1536 worked MetaMathQA problems, 768 source BoolQ labels, 256 ten-document HotpotQA cases, 1074 real prior typed demonstrations, 384 e-SNLI human explanations and labels, and 384 human-authored Dolly records across four instruction types. Each optimizer batch samples one complete request from each of five prespecified strata: math, judgment, reading, tools and general instructions. Normalize next-token loss per request; 65 percent of that weight is assigned to the visible reply and termination. At the first pass also predict the first visible token, with a two-way contrast on one-token yes/no replies. The second pass produces unrestricted ordinary vocabulary logits. No pass receives a gold slot or result during serving. There is one short model object and one adapter for plain requests and APIs. No router selects between tool and reasoning experts. Delegate earlier qualified explicit evidence format or long plain inputs at 16384 tokens to the checked parent 04 runtime. In a cold single-stream direct pair score 24 fresh ASDiv/SVAMP items, 24 new balanced BoolQ passages, 24 additional human Dolly questions with original contexts and short independently supplied answers, all 50 archived field requests and all 22 public executable items. The individual model sees every ordered question with the same true callback catalog, initial token IDs, thinking and free 384-token/three-turn policy. Each Dolly answer must match the normalized publisher string for primary success; also report source-phrase content. Eval contexts excluded from Dolly fitting, no fivegram near matches above 0.30 in response dataset questions with test prompts, prior public cases are retention only. Compare full final content, actual grounded execution, per-request first/total seconds and peak MLX bytes. Count the physical identity of the unified module, two distinct final-layer KV states and all global cache offsets. This short-stream study does not qualify full-length deployment of the new policy.
gate: Require 14 net more completed-correct mixed outcomes than Base, exact paired and shared-resource randomization p<=.05, six net gains on the 72 new human requests and at least one gain in each of new word problems, binary passage judgments and user-authored extraction. All enrolled families must equal or beat Base on correct answers, completed correct outcomes and completion. Require 12 net more grounded actions, every previously correct task in both 50-request release and 22-call public retention panels, and strictly lower first-token sum, end-to-end sum and native peak. The same model object must serve both short modes, seven distinct native attention histories and the cached vs full last-token top decision must agree with max logit deviation <=.6. Stop at the first pair or the resource ceiling. Any missed criterion closes this fit. A pass licenses an equal-exposure one-application trained control and a new isolated 128K retention and field replication before release.
